item.title: “Taghi of Curaçao” goes on trial for numerous murders
item.description:
“Taghi of Curaçao” goes on trial for numerous murders

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A gang leader dubbed the “Taghi of Curaçao” by prosecutors has gone on trial at the Netherlands’ high-security prison in Vught, where he is being held for his own safety.

Shurendy “Tyson” Q. is accused by public prosecutors of being one of the leaders of the No Limit Soldiers, a Curaçao gang, and of involvement in eight murders as well as several attempted killings.

Q. was extradited from Dubai in June and followed Monday’s opening hearing by video link from his cell. The prosecution is being made from Curaçao but being heard in the Netherlands, and is expected to run well into next year, with around 13 separate case files and large volumes of encrypted communication still to examine.

Much of the evidence consists of encrypted messages that prosecutors say were used to discuss targets, money and killings. Prosecutors told the court there was no doubt that Q. was the user of the accounts.

No Limit Soldiers gang members have been convicted of serious drug offences and murders in the Caribbean. Its members are also implicated in the 2013 murder of Curaçao politician Helmin Wiels.

In 2014, Q. was acquitted in the Netherlands after judges found prosecutors had not proved he was behind a set of intercepted messages. The next hearing is on 27 November.

item.title: US transgender woman returns home after failed Dutch asylum bid
item.description:
US transgender woman returns home after failed Dutch asylum bid

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A transgender woman from the US who sought asylum in the Netherlands has returned home after her application bid failed and she suffered serious intimidation at the Ter Apel refugee centre.

Jane-Michelle Arc, from California, was one of approximately 76 Americans that sought asylum in the Netherlands last year. She flew to Schiphol airport and was instructed by customs officers to report to the immigration service IND at Ter Apel, which houses roughly 2,000 asylum seekers.

Her reason for leaving the US was the change in policy enacted by the Trump administration, which in an executive order denounced “ideologues who deny the biological reality of sex”, and ended the federal recognition of any gender identity besides male and female, rolling back anti-discrimination policies and protections on employment, housing and healthcare protections for trans people.

But the conditions at Ter Apel, which Arc described as “dire”, were life-threatening, she said, citing anti-trans hostility from other people at the camp.

Dangerous conditions 
“This is the dumbest thing I’ve ever done”, Arc told the Guardian. “The situation I have in the US as a trans person, not good, right?. But here, I will be hurt or killed,” she separately told outlet Powned last month.

She said it was too dangerous to even walk to the supermarket, and spoke of the rising violence around the centre that has occurred this summer amid an overflow of refugees who were sleeping outside the facility gates in the heat.

After numerous fights, including two stabbings, aid organisations temporarily stopped working there for their own safety. Asylum minister Bart van den Brink subsequently enacted new measures including more security guards, CCTV cameras, and rooms for people without beds at the centre to stay indoors during the day.

US asylum claims 
Arc estimated there are roughly 35-50 other trans people at the centre, housed in a special block away from other residents. It is unclear how many are seeking asylum on the grounds of gender discrimination, but Dutch group LGBT Asylum Support said in mid-2025 it was assisting around 20 US trans individuals with pending asylum claims.

“The IND generally states that discrimination by authorities and fellow citizens can be considered an act of persecution if it is so severe that victims can no longer function socially and societally,” the group said in a statement reported by Reuters.
“But the IND maintains that there are no grounds for exceptional treatment of transgender and queer refugees from the US.”

Another US asylum seeker, Lisa Gayle Carter-Stewart, who fled Montana with her 14-year old transgender daughter said their application was automatically rejected because America is considered a safe country, according to the Guardian.

The IND dismissed her daughter’s statement that they would commit suicide if forced to return to the US, Carter-Stewart said. Her daughter did not feel safe to ever leave her room at Ter Apel and attempted suicide three times while staying there, before they were moved to a more family-friendly camp near Leiden. Despite their experiences in the Dutch camps, they still feel unsafe returning to the US.

item.title: More than 500 complaints of discrimination during WorldPride
item.description:
More than 500 complaints of discrimination during WorldPride

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

More than 500 reports of discrimination were received by a volunteer hotline during last week’s WorldPride event in Amsterdam.

The online portal RITA (Report It Always), set up for members of the LGBTQI+ community, said reports were still coming in following the two-week event, which included the city’s annual Pride canal parade on August 1.

Altogether 520 discriminatory incidents were reported, including 74 last weekend as the festivities drew to a close.

Co-founder Jerrald Justin told RTL Nieuws the figures were a “sad success” that reflected his organisation’s efforts to raise its profile during WorldPride.

This year RITA set up 35 ”safe spaces” around the city, including hotels, the Stedelijk Museum and the Nieuwe Kerk, where people could seek shelter from discrimination and report incidents in confidence.

The figures are hard to compare with previous years because WorldPride was a bigger event than the one-day canal parade, attracting more visitors, while RITA’s publicity campaign also led to more reports.

“Behind those 520 reports are 520 people who wanted to have a nice day but didn’t,” Justin said.

He told NOS the figures showed that much still needed to be done to highlight and combat homophobia. “It always starts with swearing and heckling and ends with violence,” he said. “We need to think of something together.”

item.title: Drought could force football clubs to delay start of season
item.description:
Drought could force football clubs to delay start of season

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Amateur football clubs face having to cancel fixtures in the opening weeks of the season because the drought has made pitches unplayable.

The Delfland water authority has imposed a sprinkler ban across an area covering Delft and the Westland region, while the council has told them not to play on grass until the ban is lifted.

“We have 11 football pitches, but we can only use the three that have artificial surfaces,” Dick Hartman, secretary of FC ’s-Gravenzande told NOS.

“There is a chance that matches can’t go ahead,” he said. “We are doing a rain dance every day in the hope that it rains.”

The Dutch football association KNVB sent clubs a letter on Monday ahead of the start of the second and third division seasons, which kick off this weekend.

It urged clubs to “move matches to available artificial pitches if possible” and spread matches across the weekend to conserve grass surfaces. Otherwise clubs will have to apply to postpone matches using “the regular procedure”.

Jean Demollin, chair of southern Limburg club SNC ’14, said it was a struggle to keep the pitches in shape for training. “When the league matches start it will get worse,” he said. “We’ll have to move games or start with away fixtures. We haven’t got to that point yet, but I fear the worst.”

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Nine people have arrested after police seized 586kg of drugs in a raid in a coastal suburb of The Hague.

Armed police guarded the entrance to a block of flats in Zeezwaluwhof, in Duindorp, on Thursday, as officers spent several hours searching the building.

Six people were arrested at the time of the search and three others in the following days. All but one are in custody pending a first court appearance on Wednesday.

The public prosecution service did not release further details of the suspects or charges, citing the ongoing investigation.

item.title: Hackers access Dutch credit card data in latest cyberattack
item.description:
Hackers access Dutch credit card data in latest cyberattack

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Simian, a Groningen-based company that owns a number of budget printing brands has warned customers in the Netherlands and Belgium that their personal details may have been stolen in a cyberattack.

In an email to affected customers, the company said attackers may have accessed email addresses and hashed passwords stored in its customer files.

Simian says on its website that it serves around 500,000 customers across its three brands Reclameland, Drukland and Flyerzone.

It has not said how many were affected by the breach, but that only a small number of customers had their credit card details intercepted. Those customers were contacted individually by phone and email, according to ANP.

Simian said it had reported the breach to the Dutch data protection authority AP and filed a report with police. It has brought in a specialist cybersecurity firm to investigate.

The company also said the leak did not originate in its own systems, but at an external service provider.

It confirmed the incident was not connected to the recent breach at CEVA Logistics, the delivery firm whose hack exposed customer data at Bol, De Bijenkorf, Ajax, ING and Ace & Tate.

The attack is the latest in a run of data breaches at Dutch companies, following the CEVA incident and, earlier this year, a mass hack at telecoms provider Odido.

item.title: “Easiest title so far” says Schilder after dominating shot final
item.description:
“Easiest title so far” says Schilder after dominating shot final

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Jessica Schilder retained her European shot put title with a dominant performance as the Dutch team picked up three medals on the first day of the championships in Birmingham.

The 27-year-old from Volendam threw down a gauntlet in the opening round with a throw of 19.81 metres and improved three more times to reach 20.72 with her final throw.

Team-mate Jorinde van Klinken took the silver medal with a personal best of 19.64m in the opening round, while the third Dutch competitor, Alida van Daalen, also reached the final, finishing in 11th place with 17.54m.

All five of Schilder’s legal throws were further than Van Klinken’s best effort as she became the first woman since 1974 to win a hat-trick of European titles.

“I shouldn’t say it, but I think this was actually the easiest title so far,” Schilder told NOS afterwards. “I’m very grateful for this competition and I secretly enjoy it, but I’d rather train 100 times because I can’t stand the tension of competing. It’s real torture.”

The mixed relay team completed an opening-day set for the team by taking the bronze medal, leaving the Netherlands second in the medal table.

Relay bronze

The Dutch were without anchor specialist Femke Broeders-Bol, who is concentrating on her new event, the 800 metres.

Lieke Klaver opened up a clear lead on the opening leg which the Netherlands retained with Jonas Phijffers and Terrence Agard, but anchor runner Myrte van der Schoot was overtaken in the final straight by the Norwegian and British runners.

“We ran very well with a new team,” said Klaver. “I’m really proud of everyone.”

Mahadi Abdi Ali finished a creditable sixth in the men’s 5000m final, behind the Norwegian Jakob Ingebrigtsen, who won his seventh European title at the age of just 25.

“I ran the race of my life,” said Abdi Ali, who was in contention for a medal going into the final straight, finishing just two seconds behind the winner.

Foppen’s fall

But there was disappointment for Mike Foppen, who was running strongly when he fell twice as the field bunched in the closing laps.

Foppen got up to finish 11th, just behind team-mate Tim Verbaandert. “There was a medal in it for me if I hadn’t fallen,” he said. “I’m in the form of my life.”

Broekers-Bol will start her quest for gold in the 800 metres heats on Tuesday morning, while Ruben Rolvink and Shaquille Emanuelson will try to qualify for the men’s discus final.

Later in the day Nadine Visser will be hoping for a medal in the 100 metres hurdles.

item.title: House prices drop in six councils in three months
item.description:
House prices drop in six councils in three months

August 11, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The price of homes fell in six Dutch councils in the second quarter of 2026, up from just one three months earlier, a sign that the housing market is levelling off.

Figures from national statistics agency CBS and the Land Registry showed the biggest drop was in Noord-Beveland, in Zeeland, where prices were 5.1% lower than a year earlier.

Prices also fell in Ouder-Amstel (-2.8%), Hillegom (-2.5%), Valkenswaard, Veldhoven and IJsselstein. In the first quarter, only Gulpen-Wittem in Limburg had seen a fall.

Nationally, prices were still 4.2% higher than a year earlier – the tenth quarter in a row of increases, though the pace has slowed.

The sharpest rises were in the rural east and north. Prices in Oost Gelre, in Gelderland, jumped 20.9%, followed by Voorst (19.4%) and Pekela (16.2%).

Among the four biggest cities, prices in Amsterdam rose 0.1%.

item.title: Police investigating three explosive attacks on pilates studio
item.description:
Police investigating three explosive attacks on pilates studio

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A pilates studio in Gelderland has been hit by three explosive attacks in six weeks, the most recent in the early hours of Monday, police have said.

The studio in Zevenaar, which opened a year ago, was first targeted on June 24, when a blast blew a window pane out of the front door and caused a fire to break out.

A witness saw a man in black clothing and a cap running from the scene immediately after the explosion, but police have not managed to trace him.

Five days later a second explosion blew a hole in the entrance. The word betalen (“pay”) was written three times on a window.

The most recent attack was at around 2.45am on Monday, when another explosion went off and a brick was hurled through a window, Omroep Gelderland reported. The explosion was heard throughout the neighbourhood.

The door and several windows of the building have been boarded up following the attacks. Police would not say if they were linked or if any arrests have been made.

item.title: Two men suspected of helping grave robber sell stolen valuables
item.description:
Two men suspected of helping grave robber sell stolen valuables

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Two men have been questioned on suspicion of acting as accomplices for a man accused of stealing valuables from a cemetery in The Hague by selling the items to a gold dealer.

The 60-year-old man, who works as a shift manager at the city’s main cemetery on Kerkhoflaan, was arrested in June after police received a tip-off that items such as jewellery and gold fillings had been stolen during working hours.

The prosecution service confirmed on Monday that two other people who worked at the cemetery were suspected of money laundering “by selling valuable objects originating from the cemetery”.

The man was arrested after an inspection of the official register where second-hand and antique traders are required to log their purchases revealed that he had sold several items to a gold exchange bureau.

Prosecutors said there were no indications from the investigation so far that items had been stolen from other cemeteries in the city. The inquiry covers the period from 2023 until the man’s arrest.

The city council has launched its own internal inquiry and set up a hotline for families who were concerned that their relatives’ valuables may have been stolen. So far the hotline has received around 60 calls.
